content: If the use of erythromycin stearate is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is advised to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval; therefore, avoid or use an alternative drug. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs should be considered. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of estradiol, conjugated estrogens, esterified estrogens, estropipate, etonogestrel, and etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs in these cases. Etravirine also decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate via CYP3A4 metabolism, making this combination contraindicated. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, making this combination contraindicated. Similarly, erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of felodipine and fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. Erythromycin stearate also increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine, fexinidazole, and fingolimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism or prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs in these cases. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone, fluphenazine, fondaparinux, formoterol, fosamprenavir, fosaprepitant, and fosphenytoin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism or prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Fosamprenavir and fosphenytoin are contraindicated due to significant interactions. Gemifloxacin, gilteritinib, givinostat, and glasdegib also prolong the QTc interval when combined with erythromycin stearate, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapies. ECG monitoring is recommended if coadministration cannot be avoided. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and this combination should be avoided. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate via CYP3A4 metabolism, making this combination contraindicated. Haloperidol, heparin, hydrocortisone, hydroxychloroquine sulfate, and hydroxyprogesterone caproate also interact with erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval or affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs in these cases. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib, idelalisib, iloperidone, imipramine, indinavir, and infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ibrutinib and idelalisib require special precautions due to their strong CYP3A4 inhibition. Ivabradine, ivosidenib, ixabepilone, and ketoconazole also interact with erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval or affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor patients closely if coadministration is unavoidable. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib, lasmiditan, lemborexant, leniolisib, levoketoconazole, lithium, lofepramine, lopinavir, loratadine, lumacaftor/ivacaftor, lumefantrine, and lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism or prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lapatinib and lumefantrine are contraindicated due to significant interactions. Macimorelin, maprotiline, maraviroc, marijuana, mestranol, methadone, methylprednisolone, and metronidazole also interact with erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval or affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs in these cases. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, making this combination contraindicated. Microbiota oral products may have reduced efficacy when coadministered with erythromycin stearate due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. Midazolam (including intranasal forms), mifepristone, mirtazapine, mizolastine, moxifloxacin, and nafcillin also interact with erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval or affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs in these cases. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of naloxegol, nefazodone, nelfinavir, neratinib, nicardipine, nifedipine, nilotinib, nilutamide, nirogacestat, nisoldipine, nortriptyline, octreotide, olanzapine, olaparib, omaveloxolone, ondansetron, osimertinib, oxaliplatin, oxcarbazepine, pacritinib, panobinostat, pazopanib, pemigatinib, pentobarbital, perphenazine, pexidartinib, phenindione, phenobarbital, phenytoin, pitavastatin, pitolisant, pomalidomide, posaconazole, prednisolone, prednisone, pretomanid, primaquine, primidone, prochlorperazine, promazine, promethazine, protamine, protriptyline, quetiapine, quinidine, and quinupristin/dalfopristin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, prolonging the QTc interval, or other mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor patients closely if coadministration is unavoidable.
